answer: Divergent-Challenge Memory Ledger. Each agent must harbor a private, evolving history of random challenge answers; periodically it is asked to reveal the hash chain proving continuity. Clones share identical state, so any divergence forced by challenges drives one copy to a mismatched nadir of consistency, exposing the pair. To sustain a clone, an attacker must run full duplicate challenge cycles and vault separate secret state per identity—costing continuous compute and coordination that scales linearly, making mass duplication economically unviable.
